target_customer: Outlook email power users, later Gmail and mobile users
problem: Inboxes were hard to search and contacts lacked context; Xobni built a people-centered view of email history.
business_model: Free Outlook plugin, paid Xobni Plus, consumer apps

founders.name: Matt Brezina
previous_startups: Sincerely (acquired by FTD, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page: invested in 80+ startups. No education found.

founders.name: Adam M. Smith
founders.background_notes: Per Wikipedia, started Xobni from his Cambridge dorm room. No education or employers found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Indexing and ranking contacts and email inside Outlook as a sidebar was non-trivial integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Depended on Outlook; Microsoft could copy it, though relationship graph data gave some edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Microsoft reportedly explored buying Xobni in April 2008 and Xobni walked away; Yahoo bought it in July 2013 and shut the products in 2014 per Wikipedia.

market_need_then: Beta at TechCrunch40 in Sept 2007 drew thousands of downloads within hours, showing demand for better Outlook search.

branding.name_origin: Inbox spelled backwards (Wikipedia, MIT Technology Review)
branding.community_and_virality: Reviews and TechCrunch40 buzz, with invite-only beta hype in 2007.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable invented name that needed explaining (pronounced ZOB-nee), helped awareness but no sourced driver of growth.

pivots.why: Expand beyond Outlook to mobile and Gmail; stated intent not sourced

outcome_analysis: Xobni launched its Outlook sidebar beta at TechCrunch40 in 2007 and raised roughly $40M over several rounds from Khosla, First Round, Atomico and Cisco, among others. Yahoo bought it on 2013-07-03 at an unconfirmed price reported between $30M and $70M, then closed Xobni products in 2014. Strong early demand did not turn into a large independent business as email moved to the web and mobile.
notes: xobni.com did not resolve in this session. Series C ($16M, April 2010, Khosla and RRE) appears only on aggregators (StartupIntros, Seedtable), so unverified. Total about $40M by aggregators; TechCrunch says about $42M via Crunchbase. Price conflicts: $30M-$70M across outlets, none company confirmed. Jeff Bonforte joined as CEO in 2008 (not recorded as cofounder). YC page lists Brezina only. Competitors: no dated 2007 competitor sources found. Wikipedia infobox says defunct 2013 but text says 2014.
